items.q: How was this website built?
items.a: It is a static site on GitHub Pages. An hourly GitHub Action fetches his GitHub data, embeds all content with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and writes a vector index and a question bank as JSON. In the browser, answers come from that index; on devices with WebGPU a small open LLM (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct via WebLLM) rewrites them conversationally. No server and no paid API.

items.q: How does this chatbot work?

If your device supports WebGPU it also runs a small open LLM in your browser to phrase the answer. It only answers from Sahaj's data and links the source.

items.q: Why does the site look like a transformer?
items.a: The concept is "Attention Is All You See": every word is a token, the hero is generated by sampling, hovering a word shows attention to related words (real embedding similarity), scrolling moves deeper through the layers (one per section and one per project), and his work sits on a latent-space map.

items.q: Does this site track visitors?
items.a: There are no cookies, no analytics and no tracking scripts, and the site stores nothing about you on any server. One thing does leave your browser: when a page opens, it asks the free service api.ipify.org for your public IP address and shows it back to you in the address bar (for example /ip=203.0.113.9) and in the footer. This site does not store or log that address. It is kept only for the current browser session and is gone when you close the tab. If you would rather not use it, block api.ipify.org (for example with an ad blocker) and the site works the same without it.

items.q: What is the ip= part of the URL?
items.a: Your own public IP address, as reported by api.ipify.org when you opened the page. It is added to the address bar without reloading the page. Be aware that it is then part of the URL, so it appears in your browser history and in screenshots, and anyone you send that exact link to will see it. If someone opens a link that contains another person's address, the site replaces it at once with their own.

items.q: Does the site change depending on who I am?
items.a: A little, and only in your browser. At the start it reads harmless context (time of day, device type, language, light or dark mode, where you came from, and whether you have visited before) and a simple hand-written rule set, not a trained model, guesses whether you are probably a recruiter, a developer, a researcher or just curious. It then adjusts the greeting, the order of the sections and the second button in the top section. The guess is only a heuristic and often says "curious" because many apps hide where a visit came from. You can correct it with "not you? switch" under the headline. The guess is worked out in your browser and kept only for the current browser session; the only thing that leaves your browser is the public IP lookup described above.

Each pulse is a real file finishing loading (fonts, scripts, data, the portrait), the log lines carry real sizes and counts, and the greeting at the end is decoded token by token. At the end the network collapses into the first letters of the headline. It plays once per session, and you can click or press any key to skip it.

items.q: What is Sleep-Consolidating LLM?
items.a: Sleep-Consolidating LLM is a continual-learning research project (2026). A language model learns nothing from what happens after training. An agent can keep notes, but the model itself either never absorbs them or, once fine-tuned on them, forgets older skills. Can it "sleep": turn a day's notes into weights without losing what it already knew? Each simulated day a 4-bit Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct reads documents from a seeded synthetic world of names it cannot know (about 20% of facts are later updated) and writes atomic notes.

items.q: How does Sleep-Consolidating LLM work?
items.a: Each simulated day a 4-bit Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct reads documents from a seeded synthetic world of names it cannot know (about 20% of facts are later updated) and writes atomic notes. At night it dreams: grounded question-answer pairs (answer-first), paraphrases and counterfactuals, de-duplicated and selected for diversity. One rank-16 QLoRA adapter is trained on a mix of 40% dreams from earlier nights, 20% ARC-Easy, HellaSwag and GSM8K train items and 40% new dreams, with a KL-to-base penalty on the replay part. QA is scored on held-out phrasings with no notebook.
